subject: error correlation for a system of linear models

messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: error correlation for a system of linear models
parts:
Hi all,

Would really appreciate a bit of modelling help:

I’m trying to fit a system of single variate models:

y_1 ~ normal (beta_1 * x_1, sigma_1)
y_2 ~ normal (beta_2 * x_2, sigma_2)
....
.....
y_D ~ normal (beta_D * x_D, sigma_D)

where 
x_1, ... , x_D and y_1, ... , y_D are data
beta_1, ..., beta_D, sigma_1, ... , sigma_D are parameters to be estimated

If I want to check to what extends the residuals (sigma’s) are correlated, what’s the best way to approach this?

Many thanks,

Andy

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] error correlation for a system of linear models
parts:
You could fit a covariance matrix for the noise.

y ~ multi_normal_cholesky(beta * x, L_Sigma);

We recommend doing it with a Cholesky factor composed of
a scaled LKJ prior as discussed in the regression chapter of
the manual.

The usual notion of residual is (y_d - beta_d * x_d). You
could just look at correlations of the residuals for the data.
You even get a posterior estimate if you do it in generated
quantities.

- Bob
